title: PVC Drain-Waste-Vent Layout and Glue in a Master Bathroom (This Old House)

locations.name: Master bathroom (upstairs)
locations.basis: Transcript states the plan is to run plumbing to the master bathroom above the crew’s location and describes fixtures (toilet, tub, lavatory, shower) in that space.

summary: This Old House demonstrates planning and installing a PVC drain-waste-vent (DWV) run in a master bathroom. The host outlines typical pipe sizes by fixture (3" for the toilet, 2" for the shower, 1.5" for the lav/vent) and reviews a range of fittings and angles (90° and 45° elbows, plus 60° and 22° variants; street side/male-to-female adapters for tight spaces). The video covers layout considerations, including drilling holes upstairs, dry-fitting with hangers, and ensuring proper pitch. It then covers joint preparation with cleaner and cement, marking witness lines, and performing a quick-set cementing process (five seconds) to ensure solid, drip-free connections for the tub, toilet, lavatory, and shower later in the project.
